structural_updates.body:
## Delivery objective: continue to working end-to-end mailboxes

The maintainer explicitly asked to finish mailboxes end-to-end without routine permission-to-continue checkpoints. The archive/model stopping point is therefore **not the product endpoint**.

The active lifecycle test-model slice will finish its validation and final review as an internal quality gate. **No additional standalone-model sequence is planned.** Next work is the smallest coherent behavior-bearing production integration, reconciled against current main (at least `f8b4f4c8ee13ee009dc66b4444d8c00d33705e39`), rather than importing the whole frozen candidate or treating it as current source.

The immediate milestone remains: **A explicitly publishes an encrypted result → an independently authorized destination commits durable acceptance → A exits → separately admitted B receives and explicitly ACKs**, including restart, lost-ACK, retry and refusal coverage. Stdout is not the result channel. This is a milestone toward the full bidirectional Call/Cast/Reply and unattended product scope under #4622/#5544, not a redefinition of completion.

Continuous implementation, testing, review and fixes can proceed within the approved architecture. Genuine unresolved authority allocation/transaction or security-boundary changes will be surfaced together with concrete recommendations, not smuggled into helper APIs or new tokens. S/U, existing `mvm-hostd`/no new crate, keylessness, original scoped custody and strict current-generation/disclosure/completion rules remain intact.

No installation/linger/root-service change, secret exposure, cloud spending, destructive cleanup, unqualified native action or code landing is implied. Implementation PRs remain reviewable changes; production/backend/security/density acceptance boxes stay open until the corresponding evidence exists. Design PR #5648 is separately merged; that does not activate mailbox runtime behavior.

The narrow signed-V3-selector/pre-effect-refusal ownership scope is now [recorded under canonical service owner #4629](https://github.com/tinylabscom/mvm/issues/4629#issuecomment-6937564728). It includes only the required MailboxGrant selector compatibility seam and original-admission/key-derivation consumers; it does not supersede the existing public API, guest/service or journal contribution boundaries. #5328 is closed as superseded by merged #5377, not a pending interface prerequisite.

This safety slice proceeds alongside the concrete DEST preallocation/current-authority contract needed for the positive A→DEST→B path. No new wire/refusal/signing-purpose approval or production activation follows, and no acceptance checkbox is completed by the coordination record.

## Maintainer decision: build a bounded destination-scoped authority role

The maintainer approved the recommendation to **build this role under its stated security requirements, not to approve production activation**. Unsupported paths continue to refuse until their required guarantees are implemented and evidenced.

### Approved responsibility

- One explicitly identified, bounded, address-scoped destination-authority role in **existing `mvm-hostd`; no new crate**. It is originated and reaped by the qualified user-manager service integration, not adopted by PID or frontend detachment.
- The authority owns only that DEST's purpose-separated receipt/history/anchor custody and the sole canonical destination transition writer. It receives no payload decryption keys, sender keys, general issuer authority or sign-arbitrary-bytes interface.
- The shared scheduler remains entirely keyless. Endpoint payload custody remains independently scoped. Active authority holders are admission-bounded; their density and performance cost must be measured.
- DEST is explicitly preallocated before A sends, with approved enrollment and a stable history identity independent of A/B VM lifetimes. Send does not implicitly allocate it. B later attaches under independent current admission, Receive authority and key possession; no fabricated pre-B boot.

### Required implementation boundaries

Reuse the canonical mailbox custody/journal/service program and preserve #4629/#4630 contribution ownership; no second queue or policy database. Distinguish explicit provision from existing-only recovery. Acceptance, attachment, leases, ACKs and applicable effective authorization changes must be ordered by the same authoritative transition writer. Upstream owners must participate in the required ordering, or affected strict-currentness operations refuse; a snapshot, file refresh or scheduler mutex is insufficient.

Authoritative durable history/anchor commit precedes an acceptance receipt. Signing failure leaves the committed outcome with receipt pending. Exact authorized recovery preserves the original outcome/signature and does not debit again. Missing or corrupt established history/anchor/key refuses rather than generating replacement genesis. The authority verifies required storage durability itself; a scheduler's stored acknowledgement is insufficient.

This role decision does not by itself close pre-B endpoint key provisioning/release, source first-disclosure fencing, A-over-B completion, original VM ownership, or unattended platform qualification. Separate processes under one UID are not assumed to provide key-access confinement. The actual filesystem/memory/IPC/environment boundary, crash/restart exclusion and finite resource profile require implementation and evidence.

### Execution scope

Proceed with focused design/implementation review, real production consumers, regression/crash tests and reviewable changes without routine permission-to-continue checkpoints. No additional standalone-model sequence is planned. No service installation, enabling linger, macOS system-domain/admin fallback, cloud spending, secret exposure, unqualified native activation or direct code landing is implied. No implementation/security/performance acceptance checkbox is completed by this architectural approval.

## Scoped validation checkpoint — private scheduler test models

The two bounded test targets are frozen separately from production integration. They are **unmerged, uncommitted and unpublished**, and are not runtime factories or service qualification. No further standalone-model sequence is planned; work continues toward the end-to-end mailbox outcome in the [continuous-delivery record](https://github.com/tinylabscom/mvm/issues/5255#issuecomment-6937094235).

| Source | Exact identity | Validation / review |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/mvm-hostd/tests/mailbox_scheduler_profile_model.rs` | 1,000 lines; SHA-256 `113d107592fb710bd4b76372c7d6a1dc356d1ea452bf9995d672e1349cf9f63f` | 19 tests passed. The final `a..service` regression produced behavioral RED (18 pass/1 fail), followed by GREEN after checking consecutive dots in the entire unit name. Exact corrected-byte review closed the finding. |
| `crates/mvm-hostd/tests/mailbox_scheduler_lifecycle_model.rs` | 1,693 lines; SHA-256 `798cae6088c9825abaeb2c7e9f448e8028651c0e84f13bfea003436ded756b5c` | Tests-first compile RED (12 missing-method errors, not executed assertions), then 17 tests passed. Fresh complete read-only review found no actionable issue. Subsequent integration-side and final coordination passes verified all packet hashes and the one-file diff against the exact source bytes, and reviewed core transitions and boundary witnesses. Final coordination review is closed with no actionable finding; this is not integration or publication approval. |

Exact test commands were `scripts/cargo.sh test -p mvm-hostd --test mailbox_scheduler_profile_model` and `scripts/cargo.sh test -p mvm-hostd --test mailbox_scheduler_lifecycle_model`. The matching single-target Clippy commands with `-- -D warnings` and scoped edition-2024 rustfmt checks passed. Shells sourced `scripts/dev-env.sh` with `TMPDIR=/tmp`. Own-only no-index whitespace checks produced **exit 1 for a differing/new file, with zero whitespace diagnostics**; this is not reported as exit 0. Each isolated source check preserved the 4,585 inherited files unchanged. These are recorded isolated validation results, not a new full-workspace or live-service run.

The declaration target checks untrusted declarations and exact agreement only. The lifecycle target uses inert records and fake time: sticky administrative uncertainty, correlation and bounded early events, all-event deadline precedence, and separately tagged untrusted service reports. Neither grants readiness, current authorization, canonical identity, process collection, exclusion release, or automatic restart. Administrative request non-submission is not evidence about mailbox payload disclosure.

### Durable source locations

The actual source files remain in their attached source worktrees; temporary review packets are supplemental, not the sole copies. Source provenance (causal frontiers, **not Git commits**):

canonical_ownership_updates.body:
## Narrow ownership coordination: signed V3 selector and pre-effect refusal

#4629 remains the canonical Call/Cast/Reply service/API owner. The contribution boundaries documented on #5328 are preserved; this does not authorize a second service, conversation table or journal.

Current publication state matters: [#5328's closing record](https://github.com/tinylabscom/mvm/pull/5328#issuecomment-6851492826) says its interfaces were incorporated by merged #5377. #5328 is therefore not a still-open dependency. Its four-file API scope was `mvm-core/src/mailbox.rs`, `mailbox/transport.rs`, `mailbox/transport/tests.rs` and `tests/mailbox_crypto.rs`; it did not assign all canonical schema work.

For the next production-consumed safety slice, the coordinated V3 integration stream will own **only the `MailboxGrant` signed-selector compatibility change needed in `crates/mvm-contract/src/protocol/mailbox.rs`**, plus the original-admission consumer guards in client/hostd and key-derivation defense. This is a narrow task assignment, not ownership of the rest of that schema or #4629's API work. Any actual overlapping patch must be reconciled before editing its scope.

Required behavior: preserve original signed selection through decoding/config conversion; reject selected-but-unavailable V3 before VM, console, plaintext or host-key derivation effects; preserve absent-field legacy serialization and V1/V2 meanings. Tests must drive the real pre-effect consumers and compatibility fixtures.

This does **not** freeze a new Call/Cast/Reply envelope, guest frame, wire refusal enum, signing purpose, positive authority factory or destination allocation contract. The #5647 conversation-core reconciliation remains separate. No completed behavior, test result, native qualification or acceptance-box closure is claimed by this assignment.

The maintainer approved [building the bounded destination-scoped authority role](https://github.com/tinylabscom/mvm/issues/5255#issuecomment-6938079069) in existing `mvm-hostd`, with no new crate. It owns DEST-only receipt/history/anchor custody and canonical destination transitions; the shared scheduler stays entirely keyless and payload keys stay endpoint-owned. This is an explicit additional role decision, not a widening of a tenant signer or a prolongation of the legacy VM-bound helper.

Implementation must preserve the existing canonical service/API, guest and journal ownership boundaries. Finite holder limits, strict currentness ordering, commit-before-receipt and existing-only recovery are required. Approval is for building and qualifying the role—not production activation, installation, a new wire/signing schema by implication, or completed delivery/density/security acceptance. Full detail and remaining gates are in the decision record above.

Narrow extension to the [signed-selector ownership scope](https://github.com/tinylabscom/mvm/issues/4629#issuecomment-6937564728): adding the MailboxGrant field requires exactly two mechanical exhaustive-literal updates on main `77a91c3fe0cd6ed24f01eea6ddd26ac5f67b3ab8`: `crates/mvm-core/src/mailbox/transport/tests.rs:563–569` and `crates/mvm-core/src/mailbox/journal.rs:523–529` (`verify_recovered_lease`). The integration stream may add only `service_blind: None` at those two locations. This is not a broader transfer of transport or journal ownership.

For the recovery literal, implementation/review must establish that it reconstructs legacy records only; it must not erase or normalize a signed V3 selection. Any necessary decoder/algorithm change falls outside this mechanical exception. Preserve legacy signed/serialized bytes and include the relevant recovery regression evidence. No new admission, receipt, currentness or positive V3 behavior is approved by these compatibility hunks.
